item.title: Cabbidder appoints James Sorolla as CTO to speed dispatch integrations across UK taxi sector
item.description: Cabbidder has appointed James Sorolla as Chief Technology Officer and a board member, tasking him with accelerating platform development and integrations with dispatch systems across the UK taxi and private hire sector. Sorolla will oversee enhancements to the existing Cabbidder platform and the delivery of a new Cabbidder sharing hub. item.title: TOP TAXI: Freenow opens search for London’s top black cab drivers
item.description: Image credit: Freenow by Lyft Freenow by Lyft has opened nominations for a London-focused driver recognition event aimed at celebrating black cab drivers who delivered outstanding service to passengers and communities during 2025. item.title: Out-of-area private hire driver licence revoked after ‘ghost plates’ and fraudulent insurance uncovered
item.description: A private hire driver licensed by Wolverhampton, but working in Cheltenham, has had both his driver and vehicle licences revoked after being found using illegal number plates and having previously submitted fraudulent insurance documentation, following a joint enforcement operation in Cheltenham. The incident occurred on Friday 15 November 2025 during a multi-agency taxi compliance operation held alongside Cheltenham’s November race meeting. item.title: KNIFEPOINT BILKER: Police appeal for witnesses after taxi driver held at knifepoint as fare dodger flees
item.description: Police are investigating after a taxi driver reported being threatened with a knife during an alleged fare dispute in Carlton, Nottinghamshire. According to Nottinghamshire Police, neighbourhood officers were on patrol in the area at around 2.35pm on Wednesday 28 January when they were flagged down by the driver on Gedling Road. item.title: Glasgow woman prosecuted for driving Milton Keynes licensed private hire vehicle without licence
item.description: A woman from Glasgow has been prosecuted after being found driving a Milton Keynes City Council licensed private hire vehicle without holding the required private hire driver licence. Milton Keynes City Council taxi enforcement officers were carrying out routine patrols in Wolverton on 18 October 2024 when they observed a council licensed private hire vehicle pull into a shopping area and approached the driver. item.title: Leicester to pilot new taxi rank and night-time pick-up bays near Jubilee Square
item.description: New arrangements for taxi ranks and passenger pick-up and drop-off bays will be introduced on an experimental basis in Leicester city centre from early February, as the council moves to address road safety concerns and rising late-night demand. Leicester City Council confirmed that the pilot will focus on St Nicholas Place and Highcross Street, close to Jubilee Square, an area that experiences high pedestrian and vehicle activity during evening and night-time hours. item.title: Why the 2017 ‘START AND FINISH’ rule still sits at the centre of the cross-border taxi debate
item.description: When Transport for London (TfL) set out its proposals to tackle cross-border hiring in late 2017, one idea quickly became the focal point of the debate: the introduction of a statutory requirement that every taxi or private hire journey must either start or finish in the area in which the driver and vehicle are licensed. item.title: TAXI TAX: VAT reform triggers prolonged Commons clash over rural taxi access, SEND costs and revenue risks
item.description: The recent overhaul of VAT treatment for taxi and private hire vehicle journeys prompted an extended and at times tense debate in a Commons Public Bill Committee on 29 January, as MPs from across the opposition parties warned that the measure risks higher fares, increased pressure on council budgets and unintended consequences for rural communities and vulnerable passengers. item.title: A40 Westway shut for five weeks in major TfL safety works
item.description: Image credit: TfL Transport for London will close the A40 Westway between the A40 Westway Roundabout and the Marylebone Flyover from 20 March until late April to carry out what it describes as essential safety-critical renewal works. item.title: LICENCE SURRENDERED: Uber quits Southend market weeks after green light
item.description: Uber has surrendered its private hire operator licence to operate in Southend-on-Sea, less than two months after being formally approved by the city council to enter the local market.
